newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Crean CRJ optimistic about outcome for 1996.
newsitem.headline: Crean CRJ optimistic about outcome for 1996.

text.p: Irish industrial holding company James Crean Plc said on Wednesday that it was optimistic about the outcome for 1996 as a whole.

The group said in a statement that the strong growth pattern in the poultry business is expected to continue and an improved performance from its frozen meals business for the year as a whole is expected.
"Overall a substantial increase in profits from the food division in 1996 is expected," Crean said.
Crean said demand for products in its electrical division remained soft in the UK.
But the firm said this factor was outweighed by the successful integration of the OLC business and a significant improvement in profit from the division in 1996 is expected.
The OLC group of companies, an electrical wholesaling group located in the southeast of England, was acquired in March 1996.
Crean said its print, paper and packaging division had got off to a good start in the second-half of the year and profits for the year as a whole are expected be ahead of last year.

Earlier, Crean said profit before tax for the six months to June 30 was unchanged at 9.5 million Irish pounds but added that profits after tax and minorities was up 12 percent relative to the first half of 1995.
Crean said this was a more meaningful comparison following the buyout of the minority shareholding in Irish-based industrial holding company Inishtech Plc this year.
The group said that net borrowings at June 30, 1996, excluding 31.5 million punts of convertible loan stock, were 67.7 million compared with 25.3 million at end-June last year.
Crean said sales in the food division were up 19 per cent on 1995 levels while operating profits were up 13 per cent.
"These increases were driven by the performance of the poultry business where sales were up 84 per cent and operating profits were up 40 per cent relative to last year," said Crean.
Crean said the major development in the electrical division over the first six months was the acquisition of the OLC and Arron companies.
"First time contributions from these acquisitions were mainly responsible for the 41 per cent increase in sterling sales relative to the same period in 1995," said Crean.

Crean said sales at 46 million Irish pounds in the paper, print and packaging division were up 19 per cent while operating profits at 5.3 million were up seven per cent compared to the same period last year.
"These results include a first-time contribution from the U.S. printing companies, Meridian and Elite, which were acquired at the beginning of 1996," Crean said.
The group said it was pressing ahead as rapidly as possible with substantial asset sales.

Crean said once the disposal programme has been completed, borrowings will be sharply reduced and the group will have the financial and management resources necessary to sustain a programme of expansion within the businesses that are retained.
The result will be a slimmed down and reshaped Crean with attractive growth opportunities, the company said.
-- Damien Lynch, Dublin Newsroom +353 1 6603377
